sentences.text: The petition is to quash the complaint filed for the alleged offence under Sections 17(3), 29 and 32 of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016.

2. The crux of the allegation in the complaint is that when the respondent conducted a search of the petitioner's premises, he was found to be processing and manufacturing packaged drinking water without the mandatory ISI mark and without any valid BIS (Bureau of Indian Standard) license for packaged drinking water.
3. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the complaint was misconceived; that the petitioner had not manufactured the packaged drinking water.

The petitioner had only manufactured and sold flavoured water under the name of Three Falls; that the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011 [hereinafter referred to as 'FSSAI Regulations' for the sake of convenience] clearly made a distinction between the packaged d r i n k i n g w a t e r a n d n o n - c a r b o n a t e d f l a v o u r e d w a t e r ( n o n - a l c o h o l i c ) ; t h a t https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the petitioner had obtained a license under the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI); that there was no necessity for obtaining BIS license; that the petitioner had requested for certification of their flavoured water from the BIS; that the respondent had replied by letter dated 15.01.2009 as follows;

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: There is no Indian Standard available for Flavoured Water.

Therefore, such product cannot be certified by BIS; And that, therefore, since there is a clear distinction between packaged drinking water and non-carbonated flavoured water (non-alcoholic), the Rules applicable for obtaining license from BIS for packaged water cannot be made applicable to the product manufactured by the petitioner.

The learned counsel further submitted that even in the seizure memo, the respondent had stated that they had seized twenty litres of packaged drinking water without appreciating the difference between the packaged drinking water and non-carbonated flavoured water.
Hence, the learned counsel prayed for quashing the impugned complaint.

4. The learned counsel for the respondent submitted that it is true https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis that there is a distinction made between packaged drinking water and non-carbonated flavoured water under the FSSAI Regulations, 2011.
However, the product manufactured by the petitioner is deemed to be a 'packaged drinking water' for the purpose of obtaining a license under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act.

The learned counsel would further submit that in a recent notification, the Food Safety and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Standards Authority of India had clarified that BIS license has to be obtained in addition to FSSAI license in respect of products which Mr. Manikandan Arumugam vs Bureau Of Indian Standards on 14 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97721710/
2 are shown as 'Non-carbonated water-based beverages (non-alcoholic)' without any other ingredient to escape BIS certification.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned counsel further submitted that the petitioner had a license for packaged drinking water till 31.05.2017.
However, instead of renewing the said license, he claims that he had produced and marketed a different product only to avoid obtaining a BIS license.

5. From the submissions made by the learned counsels on either side, it can be seen that there is a factual controversy as to whether the product seized from the petitioner can be called 'packaged drinking water' for the purpose of obtaining BIS license.
According to the petitioner, this product cannot be considered as 'packaged drinking water' as can be seen from the FSSAI Regulations.
According to the respondent, as per clause 3.2 of the Indian Standard specifications, the product manufactured by the petitioner is 'packaged drinking water'.
This factual dispute has to be adjudicated only before the trial Court after evidence is let in and it is determined whether the petitioner's product is a 'packaged drinking water' or not.
Hence, this Court is not inclined to https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis entertain this petition.
6. Hence, this Criminal Original Petition is dismissed.
Consequently, the connected Miscellaneous Petition is closed.
